objects.title: Group-count growth
objects.paper_statement:
The number of realized groups diverges:
\[
G_n \to \infty .
\]

objects.title: Row treatment fraction
objects.paper_statement:
For a triangular schedule array with row group count \(G_n\) and treated-group count \(G_{1n}\), where \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), the row treatment fraction is
\[
p_n=\frac{G_{1n}}{G_n}.
\]

objects.title: Stable treatment fraction
objects.paper_statement:
The treated-group fraction \(p_n\) converges to an interior limit:
\[
p_n \to p \in (0,1).
\]

objects.title: Sampling fraction limit
objects.paper_statement:
The grouped-unit fraction \(N_n/n\) converges:
\[
\frac{N_n}{n} \to \rho \in [0,1].
\]

objects.title: Bounded potential outcomes
objects.paper_statement:
There is a finite uniform outcome envelope \(B\) such that
\[
\sup_{n,i,z,A}\left|Y_{i,n}(z,A)\right| \le B < \infty .
\]

objects.title: Scaled variance nondegeneracy
objects.paper_statement:
For a feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\ge 2\), positive group counts \(G_n\), treated-group counts satisfying \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), grouped size \(MG_n\le n\), and deterministic potential-outcome schedules, there is a scaled-variance lower-bound constant \(c_\sigma\) such that \(c_\sigma>0\) and
\[
c_\sigma \le \liminf_{n\to\infty} G_n\sigma_n^2 .
\]

objects.title: Treatment-arm set
objects.paper_statement:
The treatment-arm set is the two-point set
\[
\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}.
\]

objects.title: Feasible schedule array
objects.paper_statement:
A feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\) consists of the following data:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Group size.)} A natural number \(M\) satisfying \(2\le M\).
\item \textbf{(Row sizes.)} For each row \(r\in\mathbb N\), a population size \(n_r\in\mathbb N\), a number of groups \(G_r\in\mathbb N\), and a number of treated groups \(G_{1r}\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Feasibility.)} For every row \(r\),
\[
0<G_r,\qquad M G_r\le n_r,\qquad 0<G_{1r},\qquad G_{1r}<G_r,\qquad G_{1r}\le G_r .
\]
\item \textbf{(Potential-outcome schedule.)} For every row \(r\), a deterministic potential-outcome schedule
\[
Y_r:\Omega_{n_r,M}\to \{i\in \{0,\ldots,n_r-1\}: i\in A\}\to \mathcal Z\to \mathbb R,
\]
where \(A\in\Omega_{n_r,M}\) is the realized group argument of \(Y_r\).
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Random partition design \((\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n)\)
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(\mathcal U_n\) be the finite population of \(n\) labeled units, and let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq \mathcal U_n: |A|=M\}.
\]
The group tuple \(\mathbf A_n=(A_{1n},\ldots,A_{G_n n})\) is drawn uniformly from all ordered \(G_n\)-tuples of pairwise-disjoint elements of \(\Omega_{n,M}\). Independently, the assignment vector \(\mathbf Z_n\) is drawn uniformly from all binary vectors with exactly \(G_{1n}\) treated groups.

objects.title: Group-level arm table \(h_{z,n}\)
objects.paper_statement:
For each treatment arm \(z\in\mathcal Z\) and each group \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), define the group-level arm table by
\[
h_{z,n}(A)=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{i\in A}Y_{i,n}(z,A).
\]

objects.title: Uniform slice averaging
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(M\le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}:=\{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
The \(M\)-slice design is the complete-randomization design on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), equivalently the uniform distribution over all \(M\)-element subsets of the \(n\)-unit population. For any real-valued table \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), write
\[
\mathbb E_n f
:=
\frac{1}{|\Omega_{n,M}|}\sum_{A\in\Omega_{n,M}} f(A).
\]

objects.title: PAME and estimator \(\tau_n,\widehat\tau_n\)
objects.paper_statement:
Define the finite-population partition-average marginal effect by
\[
\tau_n=\mathbb E_n\!\left[h_{1,n}-h_{0,n}\right].
\]
The difference-in-means estimator across treated and control groups is
\[
\widehat\tau_n
=
\frac{1}{G_{1n}}\sum_g Z_{ng}h_{1,n}(A_{ng})
-
\frac{1}{G_{0n}}\sum_g (1-Z_{ng})h_{0,n}(A_{ng}).
\]

objects.title: Uniform-slice \(L^2\) space
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(n\) and \(M\) with \(2M\le n\), let \(\mathcal U_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and
\[
\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq\mathcal U_n: |A|=M\}
\]
be the uniform \(M\)-slice. The space \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) is the real vector space of functions \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), equipped with uniform-slice expectation
\[
\mathbb E_n f=\binom nM^{-1}\sum_{A\in\Omega_{n,M}} f(A),
\]
inner product
\[
\langle f,g\rangle_n=\mathbb E_n[fg],
\]
and induced norm \(\|f\|_n^2=\langle f,f\rangle_n\).

objects.title: Johnson orthogonal decomposition
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(n,M\) with \(2M\le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}:=\{A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}
\]
be the uniform \(M\)-slice, let \(\mathbb E_n\) denote uniform averaging on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), and let
\[
\langle f,g\rangle_n:=\mathbb E_n[fg]
\]
be the uniform-slice inner product. For each \(k=0,\ldots,M\), let \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) be the canonical degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspace and let \(\Pi_{n,k}\) be the orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\): \(\Pi_{n,k}\) is linear, has range \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), fixes every element of \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), and satisfies
\[
\langle f-\Pi_{n,k}f,g\rangle_n=0
\qquad
\text{for every }g\in\mathcal H_{n,k}.
\]
For every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), define its Johnson components by
\[
f_k:=\Pi_{n,k}f,\qquad k=0,\ldots,M .
\]
These components satisfy the centered decomposition
\[
\sum_{k=1}^M \Pi_{n,k}f(A)=f(A)-\mathbb E_n f
\qquad\text{for every }A\in\Omega_{n,M},
\]
and distinct degrees are orthogonal:
\[
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,\ell}g\rangle_n=0
\qquad\text{whenever }k\ne \ell .
\]

objects.title: Kneser covariance \(C_{ab,n}\)
objects.paper_statement:
For a function \(f\) on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), define the normalized Kneser disjointness operator by
\[
(\mathsf K_n f)(A)
=
\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}
\sum_{C:C\cap A=\varnothing} f(C).
\]
For arm tables \(h_{a,n}\) and \(h_{b,n}\), define the ordered-disjoint covariance by
\[
C_{ab,n}
=
\left\langle h_{a,n}^{\circ},\mathsf K_n h_{b,n}^{\circ}\right\rangle_n .
\]

objects.title: Dense correction terms \(E_{\tau,1,n},R_n\)
objects.paper_statement:
Define the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm-difference table by
\[
E_{\tau,1,n}
=
\left\|\Pi_{n,1}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\right\|_n^2 .
\]
Define the independent-group leading variance scale by
\[
R_n
=
\frac{V_{1,n}}{p_n}
+
\frac{V_{0,n}}{1-p_n}.
\]

objects.title: CR2 statistic \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}\)
objects.paper_statement:
For each arm \(z\), let \(s_{z,n}^2\) be the within-arm sample variance of the observed group means, computed with denominator \(G_{zn}-1\). Define the scalar equal-group CR2 variance statistic by
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}
=
\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{G_{1n}}
+
\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{G_{0n}}.
\]

objects.title: Dense schedule class
objects.paper_statement:
The class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) consists of triangular arrays \((Y_{i,n},G_n,G_{1n})_{n\ge 1}\), with fixed common group size \(M\), for which:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feasible rows.)} The common group size satisfies \(M\ge 2\).  In each row, \(G_n>0\), \(N_n=M G_n\le n\), \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), and \(G_{1n}\le G_n\).  The potential-outcome schedule assigns a real value \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) for every group \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), every unit \(i\in A\), and every arm \(z\in\mathcal Z\).
\item \textbf{(Dense growth.)} The group count satisfies \cref{obj:ass:group-count-growth}, so \(G_n\to\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment fraction.)} The treated-group fraction satisfies \cref{obj:ass:stable-treatment-fraction}: for an interior limiting treated-group fraction \(p\), \(0<p<1\) and \(p_n\to p\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling fraction.)} The grouped-unit sampling fraction satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sampling-fraction}: for a limiting grouped-unit sampling fraction \(\rho\), \(0\le\rho\le 1\) and \(N_n/n\to\rho\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform envelope.)} The potential outcomes satisfy \cref{obj:ass:bounded-potential-outcomes}: for a uniform envelope \(B>0\),
\[
\sup_{n,A\in\Omega_{n,M},\,i\in A,\,z\in\mathcal Z}\lvert Y_{i,n}(z,A)\rvert\le B .
\]
\item \textbf{(Scaled variance.)} The exact design variance satisfies \cref{obj:ass:scaled-variance-nondegeneracy}: for a scaled-variance lower-bound constant \(c_\sigma>0\),
\[
c_\sigma\le \liminf_{n\to\infty} G_n\sigma_n^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}
=
\left\{
(Y_{i,n},G_n,G_{1n})_{n\ge 1}:
G_n\to\infty,\ 
p_n\to p,\ 
N_n/n\to\rho,\ 
\sup_{n,A\in\Omega_{n,M},\,i\in A,\,z\in\mathcal Z}\lvert Y_{i,n}(z,A)\rvert\le B,\ 
\liminf_{n\to\infty}G_n\sigma_n^2\ge c_\sigma
\right\},
\]
with the row feasibility, interiority, closed-interval, envelope, and variance-floor conditions listed above.

objects.title: Realized arm group counts
objects.paper_statement:
For \(z\in\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}\), let
\[
G_{z,n}=\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}\mathbf 1\{Z_{ng}=z\}
\]
be the number of realized groups assigned to arm \(z\) at row \(n\). Under the complete group-treatment assignment with exactly \(G_{1n}\) treated groups and \(G_{0n}=G_n-G_{1n}\) control groups, this notation gives \(G_{1,n}=G_{1n}\) and \(G_{0,n}=G_{0n}\).

objects.title: Centered arm table
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(n\) and \(M\) with \(M\le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
Given a deterministic potential-outcome schedule \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) for units \(i\in A\), arms \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and groups \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), define the centered arm-\(z\) group table by
\[
h_{z,n}^{\circ}(A)
=
h_{z,n}(A)-\mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}]
\]
for each \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), where
\[
h_{z,n}(A)=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{i\in A}Y_{i,n}(z,A),
\qquad
\mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}]
=
\frac{1}{|\Omega_{n,M}|}\sum_{B\in\Omega_{n,M}} h_{z,n}(B).
\]

objects.title: Uniform-slice norm
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(M \le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}:=\{A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
For any real-valued function \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), define its squared uniform-slice norm by
\[
\|f\|_n^2
:=
\langle f,f\rangle_n
:=
\mathbb E_n\{f(A)^2\},
\]
where \(\mathbb E_n\) denotes averaging over the uniform law on \(\Omega_{n,M}\).

objects.title: Exact Kneser covariance identity
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(M,n\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2\le M\) and \(2M\le n\). Let \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) be a deterministic potential-outcome schedule for units \(i\in A\), arms \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and groups \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), with group-level arm tables \(h_{z,n}\) as in \cref{obj:def:group-table}. Suppose the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Johnson projections.)} For each \(k=0,\ldots,M\), \(\Pi_{n,k}\) is a linear projection on functions \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\) whose range is the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspace \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), which fixes every element of \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), and whose residual \(f-\Pi_{n,k}f\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) under the uniform-slice inner product \(\langle u,v\rangle_n=\mathbb E_n[u(A)v(A)]\).
\item \textbf{(Centered orthogonal decomposition.)} For every \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\) and \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\),
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Pi_{n,k}f(A)=f(A)-\mathbb E_n f(A),
\]
and the projected components are mutually orthogonal: if \(k\ne \ell\), then
\[
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,\ell}g\rangle_n=0
\]
for all \(f,g:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum.)} For every \(k=0,\ldots,M\) and every \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\), the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator has eigenvalue
\[
(-1)^k {n-M-k\choose M-k}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the normalized Kneser disjointness operator \(\mathsf K_n\) acts on each projected component by
\[
\mathsf K_n(\Pi_{n,k}f)(A)=\lambda_{n,k}\,\Pi_{n,k}f(A),
\qquad
\lambda_{n,k}=(-1)^k\frac{(M)_k}{(n-M)_k},
\]
for every \(k=0,\ldots,M\), every \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), and every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\). Moreover, if \(f,g:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\) are centered under the uniform \(M\)-slice, then for a uniform ordered disjoint pair \((A,C)\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\{f(A),g(C)\}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\lambda_{n,k}
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,k}g\rangle_n .
\]
Finally, the ordered-disjoint covariance of the arm-difference table satisfies
\[
C_{\tau\tau,n}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\lambda_{n,k}
\bigl\|\Pi_{n,k}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\bigr\|_n^2 .
\]

objects.title: Exact PAME variance
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(n,M,G_n,G_{1n}\) be natural numbers and let \(G_{0n}=G_n-G_{1n}\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feasible partition.)} The two-stage random partition design in \cref{obj:def:random-partition-design} is feasible: \(M G_n\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Group sizes.)} \(2\le M\), \(2\le G_{1n}\), and \(2\le G_{0n}\).
\item \textbf{(Potential outcomes.)} \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) is a deterministic potential-outcome schedule, defined for every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), every \(i\in A\), and every \(z\in\mathcal Z\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
V_{z,n}
=
\operatorname{Var}_{A\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\Omega_{n,M})}\{h_{z,n}(A)\},
\qquad
C_{ab,n}
=
\mathbb E_{A}\mathbb E_{C\mid C\cap A=\varnothing}
\bigl[h_{a,n}^{\circ}(A)h_{b,n}^{\circ}(C)\bigr],
\]
and
\[
C_{\tau\tau,n}=C_{11,n}+C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n},
\qquad
R_n=\frac{V_{1,n}}{G_{1n}/G_n}+\frac{V_{0,n}}{1-G_{1n}/G_n}.
\]
For the difference-in-means estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\), the finite-population PAME \(\tau_n\), the exact design variance \(\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau_n)\), and the scalar equal-group CR2 statistic \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}\) in \cref{obj:def:cr2-statistic},
\[
\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n]=\tau_n,
\]
\[
\sigma_n^2
=
\frac{R_n}{G_n}
+
C_{\tau\tau,n}
-
\frac{C_{11,n}}{G_{1n}}
-
\frac{C_{00,n}}{G_{0n}},
\]
\[
\mathbb E[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}]
=
\frac{V_{1,n}-C_{11,n}}{G_{1n}}
+
\frac{V_{0,n}-C_{00,n}}{G_{0n}},
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}]-\sigma_n^2=-C_{\tau\tau,n}.
\]

objects.title: Dense projection limit
objects.paper_statement:
Fix a common group size \(M\ge 2\) and real numbers \(p\), \(\rho\), and \(B\).  There is a constant \(C>0\) such that, for every feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\) and every rowwise choice of Johnson projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\) on \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), the following conditions imply the displayed limits below:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Group growth.)} The array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:group-count-growth}.
\item \textbf{(Treatment fractions.)} The array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:stable-treatment-fraction} with limiting treated-group fraction \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling fractions.)} The array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sampling-fraction} with limiting grouped-unit fraction \(\rho\).
\item \textbf{(Bounded outcomes.)} The array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:bounded-potential-outcomes} with uniform outcome envelope \(B\).
\item \textbf{(Johnson decomposition.)} In every row with \(2M\le n\), the projections give the centered orthogonal Johnson decomposition
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Pi_{n,k}f(A)=f(A)-\mathbb E_n f
\]
for every \(f\) and every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), and distinct Johnson degrees are orthogonal under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum.)} In every row with \(2M\le n\), every \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\) is an eigenfunction of the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator with eigenvalue
\[
(-1)^k {\,n-M-k\choose M-k\,}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2-\bigl(R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\bigr)\to 0,
\]
\[
G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\to 0,
\]
and
\[
\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}+\frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}\to 0.
\]
Moreover, for every row \(n\), the pooled contribution of Johnson degrees \(k\ge 2\),
\[
G_n\sum_{k=2}^{M}\lambda_{n,k}
\left\|\Pi_{n,k}\bigl(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n}\bigr)\right\|_{n}^{2},
\]
has absolute value at most \(C/n\).

objects.title: CR2 phase frontier
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(M\ge 2\), and let \(A\) be a triangular array of feasible random-group experiment rows with population sizes \(n\), group counts \(G_n>0\), treated-group counts \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), grouped-unit counts \(N_n=MG_n\le n\), and deterministic potential-outcome schedules.  Fix constants \(p,\rho,B,c_\sigma\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense array.)} The array \(A\) belongs to the dense bounded schedule class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) in \cref{obj:def:dense-schedule-class}, with parameters \(p,\rho,B,c_\sigma\).
\item \textbf{(Johnson projections.)} For every row \(n\), the spaces \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) are equipped with linear projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\), \(0\le k\le M\), whose ranges are the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspaces \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), which fix functions in their ranges and have residuals orthogonal to \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).
\item \textbf{(Orthogonal decomposition.)} For every row with \(2M\le n\), every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), and every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\),
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Pi_{n,k}f(A)=f(A)-\mathbb E_n f,
\]
and distinct Johnson components are orthogonal:
\[
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,\ell}g\rangle_n=0
\qquad\text{whenever } k\ne \ell .
\]
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum.)} For every row with \(2M\le n\), every \(0\le k\le M\), and every \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\), the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator satisfies
\[
\sum_{C\cap A=\varnothing} f(C)
=
(-1)^k {\,n-M-k\choose M-k\,} f(A).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, as \(n\to\infty\),
\[
G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n \xrightarrow{p}0
\]
and
\[
G_n\bigl(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2\bigr)
-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}
\xrightarrow{p}0 .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\Pr\!\left\{
\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}/\sigma_n^2<1-\varepsilon
\right\}\longrightarrow 0 ,
\]
and the ratio \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}/\sigma_n^2\) converges in probability to \(1\) if and only if
\[
\frac{\rho E_{\tau,1,n}}{R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}}\longrightarrow 0 .
\]

objects.title: Sparse birthday consistency
objects.paper_statement:
Fix an integer \(M\ge 2\).  Then the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sparse dense arrays.)} For every feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\), if the array belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) in \cref{obj:def:dense-schedule-class} with limiting grouped-unit fraction \(\rho=0\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}\xrightarrow{p}1 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Birthday counts.)} With
\[
N_n^{\mathrm{bd}}=M\Big\lfloor \frac{n^{3/4}}{M}\Big\rfloor ,
\]
the benchmark counts satisfy \(N_n^{\mathrm{bd}}\le n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{N_n^{\mathrm{bd}}}{n}\to 0,
\qquad
\frac{(N_n^{\mathrm{bd}})^2}{n}\to\infty .
\]
\item \textbf{(Birthday-aligned arrays.)} For every feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\), if its grouped-unit count satisfies
\[
N_n=M\Big\lfloor \frac{n^{3/4}}{M}\Big\rfloor
\]
row by row and the array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:group-count-growth,obj:ass:stable-treatment-fraction,obj:ass:bounded-potential-outcomes,obj:ass:scaled-variance-nondegeneracy} for some \(p\), \(B\), and \(c_\sigma\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}\xrightarrow{p}1 .
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Eight-unit witness $\mathbf a_8$
objects.paper_statement:
The eight-unit witness fixes
\[
n=N_n=8,\qquad
M=2,\qquad
G_n=4,\qquad
G_{1n}=2,
\]
and uses the balanced sign vector
\[
\mathbf a_8=(a_1,\ldots,a_8).
\]
For every group \(A=\{j,k\}\) and every unit \(i\in A\), the potential outcomes are
\[
Y_{i,n}(0,A)=0,
\qquad
Y_{i,n}(1,A)=\frac{a_j+a_k}{2}.
\]

objects.title: CR2 software identity
objects.paper_statement:
Suppose \(M\ge 2\), \(G_{1n}\ge 2\), and \(G_{0n}\ge 2\).  Fix a deterministic potential-outcome schedule \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\), an ordered tuple \(\mathbf A_n\) of pairwise-disjoint realized groups of common size \(M\), and a balanced group-treatment assignment vector \(\mathbf Z_n\) with \(G_{1n}\) treated groups and \(G_{0n}=G_n-G_{1n}\) control groups.  Assume the software regression data satisfy the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Row identification.)} For each realized group, the \(M\) regression rows are in bijection with the units in that group.
\item \textbf{(Design matrix.)} The fitted model matrix has exactly two columns, an intercept and the numeric binary group-treatment regressor:
\[
X_{gij}
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
1\{Z_g=1\}, & j=1.
\end{cases}
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed outcomes.)} The regression outcome in row \(i\) of group \(g\) is the realized potential outcome \(Y_{i,n}(Z_g,A_g)\), and its within-group average equals the observed group mean.
\item \textbf{(Unweighted fit.)} The fit is an unweighted full-column-rank least-squares fit, with residuals \(e_{gi}\), and the average residual in each group equals the observed group mean minus the observed mean in that group's treatment arm.
\item \textbf{(Block algebra.)} The stacked cross-product satisfies \(X^{\mathsf T}X=\sum_g X_g^{\mathsf T}X_g\), the group hat matrices are
\[
H_g=X_g(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}X_g^{\mathsf T},
\]
each \(I-H_g\) is positive definite, and each CR2 adjustment \(A_g\) is symmetric positive definite with
\[
A_gA_g(I-H_g)=I.
\]
\item \textbf{(Bread scaling.)} The matrix used by the CR2 covariance calculation is \(\widetilde B=(G_nM)^{-1}B\), where \(B\) is the unweighted \({\tt sandwich::bread}({\tt fit})\) matrix.
\end{itemize}
Let \(\Sigma\) be the covariance matrix returned by \({\tt clubSandwich::vcovCR}({\tt fit}, {\tt cluster}={\tt group}, {\tt type}={\tt 'CR2'})\) in version \(0.7.0\), with \({\tt target}\), \({\tt inverse\_var}\), and \({\tt form}\) omitted, applied to this unweighted intercept-plus-treatment fit using \({\tt sandwich}\) version \(3.1\text{-}3\) for the bread.  Then the treatment-coordinate entry equals the scalar equal-group CR2 statistic in \cref{obj:def:cr2-statistic}:
\[
\Sigma_{11}
=
\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}
=
\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{G_{1n}}+\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{G_{0n}}.
\]

objects.title: Eight-unit witness moments
objects.paper_statement:
For the balanced eight-unit witness schedule with \(n=N_n=8\), \(M=2\), \(G_n=4\), and \(G_{1n}=2\), suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Johnson projections.)} There is a system of orthogonal projections \(\{\Pi_{8,k}\}_{k=0}^2\) onto the canonical Johnson harmonic spaces \(\mathcal H_{8,k}\) in \(L^2(\Omega_{8,2})\).
\item \textbf{(Centered decomposition.)} These projections decompose every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{8,2})\) after removal of its uniform-slice mean, with different harmonic degrees orthogonal under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum.)} The unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator acts on each \(\mathcal H_{8,k}\) by the eigenvalue
\[
(-1)^k {8-2-k \choose 2-k}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the witness satisfies
\[
V_{1,n}=\frac{3}{7},\qquad
E_{\tau,1,n}=\frac{3}{7},\qquad
C_{11,n}=-\frac{1}{7},\qquad
\sigma_n^2=\frac{1}{7},
\]
and, for the random partition design in \cref{obj:def:random-partition-design} and the scalar equal-group CR2 statistic in \cref{obj:def:cr2-statistic},
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}\right]=\frac{2}{7}.
\]

objects.title: One-realization observation
objects.paper_statement:
A one-realization observation \(\mathcal O_n\) at population size \(n\), common group size \(M\), realized group count \(G_n\), and treated-group count \(G_{1n}\) is a triple
\[
\mathcal O_n=(\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_n)
\]
with the following components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} \(\mathbf A_n=(A_{g,n})_{g=1}^{G_n}\) is an ordered tuple with \(A_{g,n}\in\Omega_{n,M}\) for every \(g\), and \(A_{g,n}\cap A_{g',n}=\varnothing\) whenever \(g\ne g'\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment allocation.)} \(\mathbf Z_n\) selects a subset of the realized groups with exactly \(G_{1n}\) elements.
\item \textbf{(Observed outcomes.)} For every realized group \(g\) and every unit \(i\in A_{g,n}\), \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_n\) assigns a real observed outcome \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,g,n}\in\mathbb R\).
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Independent sign prior
objects.paper_statement:
For a population size \(n\), \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) is the product finite design on arrays \(h:\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\) under which every unit-arm coordinate is drawn independently from the fair two-point law:
\[
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}
=
\bigotimes_{(i,z)\in \{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12\right).
\]

objects.title: Same-sign schedule prior
objects.paper_statement:
For each \(n\), \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) is the finite product design on Boolean schedules \(h:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{0,1\}\) whose coordinate design at every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is the fair coin design:
\[
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}
:=
\bigotimes_{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}}
\operatorname{Coin}\!\left(\frac12\right).
\]

objects.title: Rademacher mixture separation
objects.paper_statement:
Fix a common group size \(M\ge 2\).  Let \(A\) be a feasible triangular array with row population sizes \(n\), group counts \(G_n\), treated-group counts \(G_{1n}\), \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), \(M G_n\le n\), and deterministic schedules.  Let \(p\in\mathbb R\) and let \(\rho\), the limiting grouped-unit fraction, satisfy \(\rho>0\).  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Group growth.)} The array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:group-count-growth}.
\item \textbf{(Treatment fractions.)} The treated-group fractions satisfy \cref{obj:ass:stable-treatment-fraction} with limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling fractions.)} The grouped-unit fractions satisfy \cref{obj:ass:sampling-fraction} with limit \(\rho\).
\item \textbf{(Johnson projections.)} For every row \(n\), the canonical Johnson projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\) on \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) are linear orthogonal projections onto \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), fix \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), and have residuals orthogonal to \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\).
\item \textbf{(Johnson decomposition.)} For every row with \(2M\le n\), every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), and every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\),
\[
\sum_{1\le k\le M}\Pi_{n,k}f(A)=f(A)-\mathbb E_n f,
\]
and distinct Johnson degrees are orthogonal under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum.)} For every row with \(2M\le n\), every \(0\le k\le M\), and every \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\), the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator satisfies
\[
\sum_{C\in\Omega_{n,M}:C\cap A=\varnothing} f(C)
=
(-1)^k {\,n-M-k\choose M-k\,} f(A).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every row \(n\) and every statistic \(\varphi\) of the one-realization observation \(\mathcal O_n\),
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}}\mathbb E_{\mathbf Z_n}\{\varphi(\mathcal O_n)\}
=
\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}}\mathbb E_{\mathbf Z_n}\{\varphi(\mathcal O_n)\}.
\]
Moreover, under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\),
\[
V_{1,n}\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}\frac1M,
\qquad
V_{0,n}\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}\frac1M,
\qquad
E_{\tau,1,n}\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}0,
\qquad
G_n\sigma_n^2\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}\frac{1}{M p(1-p)}.
\]
Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\),
\[
E_{\tau,1,n}\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}\frac2M,
\qquad
G_n\sigma_n^2\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow}\frac{1}{M p(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M}.
\]
The two scaled-variance limits are separated by a positive gap:
\[
0<\frac{2\rho}{M},
\qquad
\frac2M\le \frac{1}{M p(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M}.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(c_\sigma\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
0<c_\sigma<\frac{1}{M p(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M},
\]
the lower-tail probabilities satisfy
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}}\{G_n\sigma_n^2\ge c_\sigma\}\to 1,
\qquad
\Pr_{\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}}\{G_n\sigma_n^2\ge c_\sigma\}\to 1.
\]

objects.title: Diagonal variance obstruction
objects.paper_statement:
Fix a common group size \(M\) with \(2\le M\), and let \(A\) be a triangular schedule array with population sizes \(n\), group counts \(G_n>0\), treated-group counts \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), \(M G_n\le n\), and deterministic potential-outcome rows.  Let \(p,\rho,B,c_\sigma\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Envelope and fractions.)} \(0<\rho\), \(1\le B\), and the array satisfies \cref{obj:ass:group-count-growth,obj:ass:stable-treatment-fraction,obj:ass:sampling-fraction} with limiting treated-group fraction \(p\) and limiting grouped-unit fraction \(\rho\).
\item \textbf{(Johnson decomposition input.)} For every row \(n\), there are orthogonal projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\) onto the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic spaces \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), \(k=0,\ldots,M\), whose positive-degree components give the centered orthogonal decomposition of every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\):
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Pi_{n,k}f
=
f-\mathbb E_n f,
\qquad
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,\ell}g\rangle_n=0
\quad\text{for }k\ne \ell .
\]
\item \textbf{(Kneser spectrum input.)} For every row \(n\) with \(2M\le n\), the Kneser adjacency operator acts on \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\) by the eigenvalue
\[
(-1)^k {\,n-M-k\,\choose\, M-k\,},
\qquad k=0,\ldots,M .
\]
\item \textbf{(Variance lower bound.)} With
\[
d_{\mathrm{same}}=\frac{1}{M p(1-p)},
\qquad
d_{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac{1}{M p(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M},
\]
the constant \(c_\sigma\) satisfies
\[
0<c_\sigma<d_{\mathrm{ind}} .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then there exist support sets \(\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) for the common-arm Rademacher prior \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) for the independent-arm Rademacher prior \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) such that both prior probabilities tend to one, every diagonal selection from either support induces an array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) with parameters \((p,\rho,B,c_\sigma)\), the conditioned one-realization laws satisfy
\[
\operatorname{TV}\!\left(
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}(\mathcal O_n\in\cdot\mid \Gamma_n^{\mathrm{same}}),
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal O_n\in\cdot\mid \Gamma_n^{\mathrm{ind}})
\right)\to 0,
\]
and the scaled exact variances converge uniformly on the respective supports:
\[
\sup_{u\in\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{same}}}
\left|G_n\sigma_n^2(u)-d_{\mathrm{same}}\right|\to 0,
\qquad
\sup_{u\in\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{ind}}}
\left|G_n\sigma_n^2(u)-d_{\mathrm{ind}}\right|\to 0 .
\]
Moreover, there is an \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every measurable one-realization variance statistic \(\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)\) satisfies
\[
\frac12
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}}
\Pr_Y\!\left(
\left|
\frac{\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)}{\sigma_n^2}-1
\right|>\varepsilon
\right).
\]

objects.title: Johnson and Kneser covariance apparatus
objects.paper_statement:
For \(0\le k\le M\), let \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\subseteq L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) be the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspace, and let \(\Pi_{n,k}\) be the \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\). For \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), the centered Johnson decomposition is
\[
f-\mathbb E_n f=\sum_{k=1}^M\Pi_{n,k}f.
\]
For \(2M\le n\), the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator is
\[
(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}f)(A)=\sum_{\substack{C\in\Omega_{n,M}\\ C\cap A=\varnothing}} f(C),
\qquad A\in\Omega_{n,M}.
\]
The normalized Kneser disjointness operator is
\[
(\mathsf K_n f)(A)=\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}
\sum_{\substack{C\in\Omega_{n,M}\\ C\cap A=\varnothing}} f(C).
\]
Its eigenvalue on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) is denoted by \(\lambda_{n,k}\). For \(a,b\in\mathcal Z\), define the ordered-disjoint covariance and the arm-difference covariance by
\[
C_{ab,n}=\langle h_{a,n}^{\circ},\mathsf K_n h_{b,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n,\qquad
C_{\tau\tau,n}=C_{11,n}+C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n}.
\]
The degree-one arm-difference energy is
\[
E_{\tau,1,n}=\|\Pi_{n,1}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2.
\]

objects.title: Johnson--Kneser adjacency eigenvalue
objects.paper_statement:
Using the uniform \(M\)-slice \(\Omega_{n,M}\), the slice function space \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), and the Johnson harmonic subspaces \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) from \cref{obj:def:johnson-decomposition}, suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Population and group size.)} \(n\) and \(M\) are nonnegative integers, with \(n\) the population size and \(M\) the common group size, and \(2M\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Harmonic degree.)} \(k\in\{0,\ldots,M\}\).
\item \textbf{(Function.)} \(f\in\mathcal H_{n,k}\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}\) be the linear operator on \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) defined by
\[
(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}f)(\Gamma)
=
\sum_{\Delta\in\Omega_{n,M}}
\mathbf 1\{\Gamma\cap\Delta=\varnothing\}f(\Delta).
\]
Then \(f\) is an eigenfunction of \(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}\) with eigenvalue
\[
(-1)^k\binom{n-M-k}{M-k}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}f
=
(-1)^k\binom{n-M-k}{M-k}\,f
\]
as an identity in \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\).

objects.title: Classical Kneser spectrum
objects.paper_statement:
For any population size \(n\) and common group size \(M\), suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(2M\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Harmonic degree.)} \(k\) is an integer with \(0\le k\le M\).
\item \textbf{(Harmonic function.)} \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\) belongs to the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspace \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator, which sums \(f\) over \(M\)-subsets disjoint from the argument, acts on \(f\) by
\[
\bigl(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M} f\bigr)(A)
=
(-1)^k \binom{n-M-k}{M-k} f(A)
\]
for every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\).

objects.title: Johnson orthogonal decomposition
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(n\) and \(M\) be nonnegative integers with \(M\le n\). For the canonical Johnson harmonic projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\) on \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), whenever \(2M\le n\), every function \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\) and every \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\) satisfy
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Pi_{n,k}f(A)
=
f(A)-\mathbb E_n f .
\]
Moreover, the projections are pairwise orthogonal: for all \(k,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,M\}\), all functions \(f,g:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), and \(k\ne \ell\),
\[
\langle \Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,\ell}g\rangle_n=0 .
\]

Boolean Hypercube*, Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.3, arXiv:1406.0142v2, pp. 10 and 12.
The cited result supplies the orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of functions on

  ∀ h2M : 2 * M ≤ n,

0b8da4868d5531ae.label: JohnsonProjections
0b8da4868d5531ae.statement:
-- @realizes \mathcal H_{n,k}(canonical inclusion-degree harmonic space)

/-- Genuine orthogonal Johnson projections onto the canonical harmonic degree
spaces, including the centered orthogonal decomposition asserted in the paper. -/
structure JohnsonProjections (n M : ℕ) where
  slice_nonempty : M ≤ n
  proj : Fin (M + 1) → (Omega n M → ℝ) → (Omega n M → ℝ)
    -- @realizes \Pi_{n,k}(orthogonal projection onto canonical degree k)
  map_add : ∀ k f g, proj k (fun A => f A + g A) = fun A => proj k f A + proj k g A
  map_smul : ∀ k (c : ℝ) f, proj k (fun A => c * f A) = fun A => c * proj k f A
  range_eq : ∀ k, Set.range (proj k) = johnsonHarmonicSpace n M slice_nonempty k
  fixes_range : ∀ k f, f ∈ johnsonHarmonicSpace n M slice_nonempty k → proj k f = f
  residual_orthogonal : ∀ k f g, g ∈ johnsonHarmonicSpace n M slice_nonempty k →
    sliceInner n M slice_nonempty (fun A => f A - proj k f A) g = 0

1a4206a6aa08dbfa.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.exact_kneser_identity
1a4206a6aa08dbfa.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:n,M,hM,h2M,J,Y,hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate,hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate), [the stated equality holds](goal). -/
theorem exact_kneser_identity (n M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (h2M : 2 * M ≤ n)
    (J : JohnsonProjections n M) (Y : PotentialOutcome n M)
    (hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate : JohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition n M J)
    (hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate : KneserAdjacencySpectrum n M) :
    (∀ (k : Fin (M + 1)) (f : Omega n M → ℝ),
      kneserOp n M (J.proj k f) =
        fun A => kneserEigenvalue n M k * J.proj k f A) ∧
    (∀ (f g : Omega n M → ℝ),
      (slice n M (by omega)).E f = 0 →
      (slice n M (by omega)).E g = 0 →
      (orderedDisjointPairDesign n M h2M).Cov
          (fun P => f P.1.1) (fun P => g P.1.2) =
        ∑ k ∈ (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin (M + 1) => 0 < k.1),
          kneserEigenvalue n M k *
            sliceInner n M (by omega) (J.proj k f) (J.proj k g)) ∧
    crossCovContrast n M (by omega) Y =
      ∑ k ∈ (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin (M + 1) => 0 < k.1),
        kneserEigenvalue n M k *
          sliceNorm n M (by omega)
            (J.proj k (fun A => armTable n M Y true A - armTable n M Y false A)) ^ 2

7c04fe7d51765a55.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.exact_pame_variance
7c04fe7d51765a55.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:n,M,G,G1,hMG,hMtwo,hG1two,hG0two,Y), [the stated variance result holds](goal). -/
theorem exact_pame_variance (n M G G1 : ℕ) (hMG : M * G ≤ n)
    (hMtwo : 2 ≤ M) (hG1two : 2 ≤ G1) (hG0two : 2 ≤ G - G1)
    (Y : PotentialOutcome n M) :
    let hG1pos : 0 < G1 := by omega
    let hG1lt : G1 < G := by omega
    let hG1le : G1 ≤ G := Nat.le_of_lt hG1lt
    let hM : M ≤ n := le_trans (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right M (by omega)) hMG
    (randomPartitionDesign n M G G1 hMG hG1le).E (pameHat Y hG1pos hG1lt) = pame n M hM Y ∧
    sigmaSq Y hMG hG1pos hG1lt =
      indepGroupVar n M G G1 hM hG1pos hG1lt Y / (G : ℝ) +
        crossCovContrast n M hM Y -
        crossCov n M hM Y true true / (G1 : ℝ) -
        crossCov n M hM Y false false / ((G - G1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ∧
    (randomPartitionDesign n M G G1 hMG hG1le).E (cr2Var Y hG1two hG0two) =
      (armVar n M hM Y true - crossCov n M hM Y true true) / (G1 : ℝ) +
      (armVar n M hM Y false - crossCov n M hM Y false false) /
        ((G - G1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ∧
    (randomPartitionDesign n M G G1 hMG hG1le).E (cr2Var Y hG1two hG0two) -
      sigmaSq Y hMG hG1pos hG1lt =
      -crossCovContrast n M hM Y

2f3a128dcf97edfa.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.dense_projection_limit
2f3a128dcf97edfa.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:M,hM,p,rho,B), [the dense projection limit result holds](goal). -/
theorem dense_projection_limit {M : ℕ} (hM : 2 ≤ M) (p rho B : ℝ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : ScheduleArray M)
      (J : ∀ r, JohnsonProjections (A.popSize r) M),
      GroupCountGrowth A →
      StableTreatmentFraction A p →
      SamplingFractionLimit A rho →
      BoundedSchedule A B →
      ∀ (hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate :
        ∀ r, JohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition (A.popSize r) M (J r))
        (hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate :
        ∀ r, KneserAdjacencySpectrum (A.popSize r) M),
      Tendsto (fun r =>
        (A.groups r : ℝ) * A.variance r -
          (A.leadingVariance r - rho * A.degreeOne (by omega) J r))
        atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      Tendsto (fun r =>
        (A.groups r : ℝ) * A.contrastCrossCov r + rho * A.degreeOne (by omega) J r)
        atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      Tendsto (fun r =>
        A.armCrossCov r true true / A.treatmentFraction r +
          A.armCrossCov r false false / (1 - A.treatmentFraction r))
        atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ r, |higherDegreeContribution A J r| ≤ C / (A.popSize r : ℝ)

c4e33a98a79b32c1.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.cr2_phase_frontier
c4e33a98a79b32c1.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:M,hM,A,p,rho,B,cSigma,J,hClass,hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate,hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate), [the cr2 phase frontier result holds](goal). -/
theorem cr2_phase_frontier {M : ℕ} (hM : 2 ≤ M) (A : ScheduleArray M)
    (p rho B cSigma : ℝ) (J : ∀ r, JohnsonProjections (A.popSize r) M)
    (hClass : DenseScheduleClass A p rho B cSigma)
    (hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate :
      ∀ r, JohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition (A.popSize r) M (J r))
    (hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate :
      ∀ r, KneserAdjacencySpectrum (A.popSize r) M) :
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb A.design
      (fun r w => (A.groups r : ℝ) * A.cr2 r w - A.leadingVariance r)
      (fun _ => 0) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb A.design
      (fun r w => (A.groups r : ℝ) * (A.cr2 r w - A.variance r) -
        rho * A.degreeOne (by omega) J r)
      (fun _ => 0) ∧
    (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → Tendsto (fun r =>
      (A.design r).Pr (fun w => A.cr2 r w / A.variance r < 1 - ε))
        atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb A.design
      (fun r w => A.cr2 r w / A.variance r) (fun _ => 1) ↔
      Tendsto (fun r =>
        rho * A.degreeOne (by omega) J r /
        (A.leadingVariance r - rho * A.degreeOne (by omega) J r))
        atTop (nhds 0))

d6406cf29681479c.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.sparse_beyond_birthday
d6406cf29681479c.statement:

c557649a7e8407fa.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.clubsandwich_cr2_consumer_identity

31daab900dd4f38d.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.rademacher_mixture_separation
31daab900dd4f38d.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:M,hM,A,p,rho,hrho,J,hGroupCountGrowth,hStableTreatmentFraction,hSamplingFractionLimit,hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate,hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate), [the rademacher mixture separation result holds](goal). -/
theorem rademacher_mixture_separation {M : ℕ} (hM : 2 ≤ M) (A : ScheduleArray M)
    (p rho : ℝ) (hrho : 0 < rho)
    (J : ∀ r, JohnsonProjections (A.popSize r) M)
    (hGroupCountGrowth : GroupCountGrowth A)
    (hStableTreatmentFraction : StableTreatmentFraction A p)
    (hSamplingFractionLimit : SamplingFractionLimit A rho)
    (hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate :
      ∀ r, JohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition (A.popSize r) M (J r))
    (hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate :
      ∀ r, KneserAdjacencySpectrum (A.popSize r) M) :
    (∀ r φ, sameObservedExpectation A r φ = independentObservedExpectation A r φ) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorSame (A.popSize r))
      (fun r u => armVar (A.popSize r) M (A.groupSize_le r)
        (samePriorSchedule (A.popSize r) M u) true) (fun _ => 1 / (M : ℝ)) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorSame (A.popSize r))
      (fun r u => armVar (A.popSize r) M (A.groupSize_le r)
        (samePriorSchedule (A.popSize r) M u) false) (fun _ => 1 / (M : ℝ)) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorSame (A.popSize r))
      (fun r u => degreeOneEnergy (A.popSize r) M (by omega) (A.groupSize_le r)
        (J r) (samePriorSchedule (A.popSize r) M u)) (fun _ => 0) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorIndependent (A.popSize r))
      (fun r u => degreeOneEnergy (A.popSize r) M (by omega) (A.groupSize_le r)
        (J r) (independentPriorSchedule (A.popSize r) M u)) (fun _ => 2 / (M : ℝ)) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorSame (A.popSize r))
      (sameScaledVariance A) (fun _ => 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p))) ∧
    FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb (fun r => priorIndependent (A.popSize r))
      (independentScaledVariance A)
      (fun _ => 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p)) - 2 * rho / (M : ℝ)) ∧
    0 < 2 * rho / (M : ℝ) ∧
    2 / (M : ℝ) ≤ 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p)) - 2 * rho / (M : ℝ) ∧
    ∀ cSigma : ℝ, 0 < cSigma →
      cSigma < 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p)) - 2 * rho / (M : ℝ) →
      Tendsto (fun r => (priorSame (A.popSize r)).Pr
        (fun u => cSigma ≤ sameScaledVariance A r u)) atTop (nhds 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun r => (priorIndependent (A.popSize r)).Pr
        (fun u => cSigma ≤ independentScaledVariance A r u)) atTop (nhds 1)

596bab13ae5b183e.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.qv_diagonal_impossibility
596bab13ae5b183e.statement:
/-- Given [the stated population sizes, design objects, functions, and conditions](hyp:M,hM,A,p,rho,B,cSigma,hrho,hB,hGroupCountGrowth,hStableTreatmentFraction,hSamplingFractionLimit,J,hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate,hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate,hcSigma), [the qv diagonal impossibility result holds](goal). -/
theorem qv_diagonal_impossibility {M : ℕ} (hM : 2 ≤ M) (A : ScheduleArray M)
    (p rho B cSigma : ℝ) (hrho : 0 < rho) (hB : 1 ≤ B)
    (hGroupCountGrowth : GroupCountGrowth A)
    (hStableTreatmentFraction : StableTreatmentFraction A p)
    (hSamplingFractionLimit : SamplingFractionLimit A rho)
    (J : ∀ r, JohnsonProjections (A.popSize r) M)
    (hJohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition_of_gate :
      ∀ r, JohnsonOrthogonalDecomposition (A.popSize r) M (J r))
    (hKneserAdjacencySpectrum_of_gate :
      ∀ r, KneserAdjacencySpectrum (A.popSize r) M)
    (hcSigma : 0 < cSigma ∧
      cSigma < 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p)) - 2 * rho / (M : ℝ)) :
    let dSame := 1 / ((M : ℝ) * p * (1 - p))
    let dInd := dSame - 2 * rho / (M : ℝ)
    QVDiagonalCertificate A p rho B cSigma dSame dInd ∧
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ S,
      (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ Filter.liminf
        (fun r => worstCaseRatioError A p rho B cSigma S ε r) atTop

e54bf255ded29f17.label: Causalean.Mathlib.Combinatorics.JohnsonKneser.kneserAdjacency_eigen
e54bf255ded29f17.statement:
/-- When [two disjoint slice-sized subsets can fit in the population](hyp:h2), [the selected harmonic degree](hyp:k), and [the given function belongs to that degree's Johnson harmonic subspace](hyp:hf), [unnormalized Kneser adjacency acts by its classical signed binomial eigenvalue](goal), for [the slice function](hyp:f). -/
theorem kneserAdjacency_eigen (h2 : 2 * M ≤ n) (k : Fin (M + 1))
    (f : SliceFn n M) (hf : f ∈ johnsonHarmonic n M k.1) :
    kneserAdjacency n M f =
      (((-1 : ℝ) ^ k.1) * ((n - M - k.1).choose (M - k.1) : ℝ)) • f

cafdac3bd1195de1.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.DenseGroupPartitionProjectionPhase.canonicalKneserAdjacencySpectrum
cafdac3bd1195de1.statement:
lemma canonicalKneserAdjacencySpectrum (n M : ℕ) :
    KneserAdjacencySpectrum n M
